added_failures_note: measured: both arms ran to their summary lines at the revisions their headers name (base bcaf26dcf 104 passed, 2 skipped, EXIT=0; head 672100e98 109 passed, 2 skipped, EXIT=0) and neither log reports a FAILED or ERROR node id, so the head log's failure set minus the base log's is empty

findings.text: the evidence table states the committed JSON Schema delta as "Pydantic model +1 field; JSON Schema +8 lines", but git diff --numstat over bcaf26dcf..672100e98 gives docs/_shared/flight.schema.json 16 added lines and 0 removed; the generator emits the property into both BackendConfig and BackendConfig__identifier_optional, as it already does for usable_input_window, which appears twice in the base file, so the eight is a one-definition figure presented as the committed delta — and the row's own claim that it was measured before either artifact was written means the scratch measurement was taken over one definition while the committed file gained two. The same figure is repeated on the manifest's artifacts line, so a reader repeated from that record cannot reconcile it either.

the slot's description says the boundary is "Measured from what the lane's own endpoint refused, never declared by the configuration", while the deliverable is a configuration slot whose only way into the system is an operator writing a value into a flight layer — and the node's own fragment says the opposite, that a lane whose recordings establish a boundary "still needs the declaration to reach the check through a configuration; the reading is the recruiter, and the slot is what lets it be written down". A reader taking the sentence literally declines to set the key, which leaves the check reachable only from a fixture — the exact gap this node closed. The sentence is mirrored into reckon/_flight_schema.py:282 and both property blocks of docs/_shared/flight.schema.json, so the contradiction is regenerated rather than confined to the source.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit over bcaf26dcf..672100e98 — b705f792f carries the production change and its tests, 672100e98 the evidence fragment — and I checked the three schema artifacts against each other directly, since the round-trip test that would compare them skips here with the LinkML generators off PATH: description, minimum and type agree in the source, the Pydantic field and both JSON Schema properties.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when asks for the slot declared in the LinkML source with both generated artifacts regenerated from it, the value carried on the recorded settings, and the gate green at head with no added failure id; the manifest's after_suite names tests/test_effective_window_slot.py plus the three pre-existing files and the arm runs to its summary line, which I re-read rather than took on the record.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is the flight-schema slot the plan's §9 followup says can land now, so that a production configuration rather than only a fixture can supply a lane's recorded refusal boundary; reckon/schema/flight.yaml:467 declares effective_input_window beside usable_input_window on BackendConfig, reckon/_flight_schema.py:282 and docs/_shared/flight.schema.json carry it in both $defs, and reckon/crew/routing.py:1556 copies it onto the recorded settings, which is the slot reachable from a configuration end to end.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at the run's manifest.md; it records the two commits, both gate arms with their log paths, the negative control and its two reddened cases, the mid-flight grant for the generator's second output with the check-manifest receipt, and one follow-on outside its write scope — and it states the JSON Schema delta as eight added lines where the committed file gains sixteen.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's orientation block, which lists six paths including docs/_shared/flight.schema.json; git diff --numstat over bcaf26dcf..672100e98 lists exactly six files, each inside that block and no seventh added or removed.

justifications.durability: the declared mutation — dropping the settings copy at reckon/crew/routing.py:1556 — reddens test_an_estimate_between_the_boundary_and_the_window_is_refused and test_the_settings_copy_carries_the_boundary_beside_the_window, and removing the field would error every positive case at load; the load case at tests/test_effective_window_slot.py:210 guards the declared type rather than the slot's presence, since an unknown key is refused at the same key path.
justifications.evidence: tests/test_effective_window_slot.py passes 5 at 672100e98, which I re-ran in the reviewed worktree in 0.60s, and its negative control reddens the two cases that depend on the settings copy; the weaker points are a committed evidence table that reports the JSON Schema delta as eight lines where git diff --numstat gives sixteen (docs/evidence/fragments/a-review-dies-where-nobody-is-looking/effective-window-slot.html:91) and a generated-artifact round-trip that skips in every worker shell.
justifications.fit: the 367 added lines return nothing under the naming checks, and the slot mirrors usable_input_window in name, position, ge/minimum_value and prose shape, as the five cases follow the surrounding pytest idiom of tests/test_routing_surface.py.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/schema/flight.yaml:467 plus reckon/crew/routing.py:1556 close the gap the section names — the check at reckon/crew/routing.py:1920 could receive the boundary only from a hand-built mapping — though the slot's own description at reckon/schema/flight.yaml:472 says the figure is never declared by a configuration it exists to be declared in.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --numstat lists six files, all inside the manifest's declared paths; the one path outside the original declaration, docs/_shared/flight.schema.json, was raised as a blocker, granted in the resume advice, and reckoned clean at head by check-manifest.log, which reads {"findings": [], "ok": true} at 672100e98.
